title: Article 355 — Duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance

content.overview: Article 355 provides that it shall be the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
content.glance: Union’s duty: protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance; ensure State government is carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
content.study:
Article 355 is a duty clause underpinning Union intervention powers, including Article 356. It links external/internal security of States with the constitutional functioning of State governments.

Examination: three limbs — external aggression; internal disturbance; constitutional functioning of State government; link Art 356.

sections.heading: Three limbs
sections.body:
1. Protect every State against external aggression.
2. Protect every State against internal disturbance.
3. Ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the duty of the Union under Article 355?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 355 provides that it shall be the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

examTips: Union duty to protect States and ensure constitutional government; foundation for Art 356.

keyTakeaways: Art 355: Union duty to protect States and ensure constitutional governance.
